definition.MODULE: API module = first path segment under /api/v1
definition.FEATURE: API resource group (first two static segments) | shared web component | background job kind
definition.MICRO_FEATURE: UI event binding (onClick, onSubmit, onChange ...) on a screen or component
definition.NANO_FEATURE: error branch: a distinct DomainError(code, message) thrown by an endpoint, an observable system response
definition.BUSINESS_RULE: exported function/class in packages/domain/src (listed under business_rules, not in the hierarchy)

entries.name: GET /health
entries.purpose: Base Health Checks Health checks are exempt from the limiter: a load balancer polling them must never be able to throttle the API into looking dead.

entries.name: POST /api/v1/auth/password
entries.purpose: Change password. Requires the current one, ends every other session (tokens issued before the change are refused by resolveSession), and returns a fresh token so this device stays signed in. Throttled like login, per account.

entries.name: POST /api/v1/auth/sign-out
entries.purpose: Sign out: end THIS session on the server, not only in the browser. Before 2026-10-11 sign-out deleted the browser's copy and nothing else, so a copied token kept working for up to 24 hours. Tokens minted before session ids existed cannot be singled out; they are reported as such and end at expiry (or with a password change).

entries.name: POST /api/v1/auth/sign-out-others
entries.purpose: Sign out of every other device, without changing the password: for a phone left behind or a shared computer someone forgot to sign out of. Same mechanism as a password change (sessions_valid_after, migration 00045): every token issued so far is refused and this device gets a fresh one minted at the cut-off. Allowed for suspended accounts, like a password change: securing an account is not something to withhold.

entries.name: GET /api/v1/auth/session
entries.purpose: Who am I, according to the server? The web app calls this on load so its idea of the session (roles, account status, profile) comes from the API, not from whatever was left in localStorage.

entries.name: POST /api/v1/candidates/work-history/:id/verify-email
entries.purpose: 2. Verify Corporate Email for Work History (F-94) — two steps.  Step 1 (no verificationCode): policy check, then a single-use 6-digit code is sent to the address. Step 2 (with verificationCode): the code proves the candidate controls the mailbox, and only then is the record marked email-verified. Previously step 1 alone marked the record verified, so anyone could claim any corporate address they could type.

entries.name: GET /api/v1/references/:refId

entries.name: GET /api/v1/candidates/:candidateId/work-history-graph
entries.purpose: 6. Get Candidate Work History Network & Graph (F-162)

entries.name: DELETE /api/v1/candidates/work-history/:id
entries.purpose: 7. Remove a role from your own work history. Before this, a mistaken entry could only be removed by deleting the whole account. Its references and any open email verification go with it (FK cascade in Postgres, applyToReadModel here); a referee's link stops working. Owner only: an administrator removing someone's record is a moderation decision with its own trail, not this route.

entries.name: GET /api/v1/internal/worker-jobs
notes: ephemeral: state held in process memory
dev/test only: returns 404 when NODE_ENV is not development or test
entries.purpose: Internal helper for inspecting async job dispatch (tests + local dev). Unauthenticated, so it exists ONLY in development and test: payloads carry user ids and, for email jobs, one-time codes and reference links. Staging and production observe the queue through the admin diagnostics.
